title: Consolidate config schemas; remove compatibility adapters and orphaned routes
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Background: Over the last three years we accumulated multiple configuration surfaces to support backwards compatibility across rollout graph versions and feature-flag aliases. There are three main pain points: (1) compatibility adapters that translate v0/v1 route manifests to the current runtime, (2) an alias table for obsolete feature flags that complicates lookup logic and UX, and (3) a set of orphaned routing entries (old rollout paths) that no longer map to any active model or shard and add noise to audits.

Goal: Flatten and consolidate configuration schemas into a single canonical profile, remove the compatibility adapter layer, collapse flag aliases into canonical flag keys, and prune orphaned routing entries. This should reduce code complexity, lower runtime allocation for the router, and simplify future rollout/versioning work.
acceptance_criteria: All compatibility adapter code paths removed from router and config loader; no runtime references remain
Configuration schema flattened to 'config.v2' with a migration tool that translates old manifests and emits warnings for unmapped entries
Flag alias table consolidated: aliases either migrated to canonical flags or marked as deprecated with TTL and migration instructions
Orphaned routing entries identified and removed after approvals; audit log of removals stored in S3 with retention policy
End-to-end regression tests pass and perf benchmark of route lookup shows <3% impact (target improvement where possible)
No active customers are using removed adapters — communications and support playbook executed
migration_plan: Run analysis job to enumerate manifests and flag usages (script: tools/config-audit v0.3) and commit a csv report to s3://redwood-config-audits/2025-02-adapter-audit.csv
Create a one-way migration utility (bin/migrate-manifest --from=v0 --to=v2) that emits mapping hints and unmapped warnings
Introduce feature gates to the runtime to toggle adapter removal for canary scoping (runtime.featureFlags.disableCompatAdapters) — default off
Canary: enable removal flag in internal staging for 48 hours, run synthetic traffic and sample customer routes, run perf and correctness checks
Gradual rollout: flip flag for 10% of traffic -> 50% -> 100% across regions, monitor errors and latency
After 100% rollout and 7 days of stable metrics, prune adapter code and delete alias records with audit entries
rollback_plan: If errors exceed threshold (>0.5% request error delta or customer complaints), flip runtime.featureFlags.disableCompatAdapters back to off (5s rollback)
If migration produced unmapped critical manifests, restore adapter code from branch 'compat-rollback-ENG-37401' and redeploy within maintenance window
Audit S3 removal logs will be retained for 90 days to allow manual restoration of pruned entries if necessary
testing_plan: Unit tests for config loader and schema validators; add negative tests for removed adapter shapes
Integration tests exercising rollout resolution using historical manifests from production (sampled set)
E2E smoke in staging with synthetic traffic replicating 95th percentile sequence length distributions
Performance benchmark: route lookup latency microbench with and without adapters (run: ci/perf/route-lookup.sh)
Safety checks: canary monitors and on-call runbook to triage mapping mismatches
implementation_notes: Consolidate parsing logic into packages/config/v2 and export a single ValidateAndNormalize(manifest) API
Remove adapter translator files in packages/config/compat/* and keep one compatibility shim branch until final pruning
Shrink router in-memory structures by removing alias indirections — update documentation for token-level cost attribution which references flag lookups
Update Console UI to consume canonical flag keys; add temporary mapping layer for UI reads if needed
Coordinate with Support/Success: prepare customer migration notes and pre-warn any accounts that reference deprecated flags
progress_updates: 2025-02-12 - Ava Martinez: Kickoff analysis completed. tools/config-audit run against last 90 days of manifests; found 1,142 manifests referencing compat shapes and ~320 orphaned routes. CSV uploaded to s3 (see links).

2025-02-18 - Ravi Singh: Prototype migration utility added in branch feat/ENG-37401-migrate-manifest. Basic mapping rules for common v0 -> v2 keys implemented. Asking infra for an isolated canary cluster for staging tests.

2025-02-22 - Design Review (Marta Li): Reviewed config schema changes; suggested adding clarifying descriptions to flags and adding translation hints in migration output. Design approved the dev proposal.
2025-02-25 - Security Review: Quick review completed; no secrets or policy infra changes required. Security requested audit log retention to be set to 90 days (updated plan).

2025-03-01 - Ravi Singh: Canary enabled in internal staging for 48 hours. Observability shows no increase in 5xxs; route lookup microbench shows 8% CPU improvement in router process. Proceeding to 10% prod canary on 2025-03-03.
notes_for_review: Please review mapping rules in platform-tools PR and suggest any missing key translations for model routing. Critical: ensure that quantization-profile overrides carried in old manifests are preserved after migration.
PM (Jordan Hsu) to confirm customer outreach plan before wide rollout; include SLA-impact checklist.
Propose deprecation TTL: 30 days for flag aliases after full rollout, then automatic deletion unless a customer case is opened.
